newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ICE rates Hungary OTP bank as "buy".
newsitem.headline: ICE rates Hungary OTP bank as "buy".

text.p: London-based brokerage ICE Securities has recommended investors to buy shares in OTP, Hungary's largest commercial bank.

"Since mid-1996 OTP shares have consistently outperformed the BUX index (of the Budapest bourse), thus both on fundamental and technical grounds we recommend purchases," ICE said in a recent company update.

The brokerage said that due to tough competition OTP had inevitably lost market share in the past few years, but it had become more efficient and competitive and was likely to retain its leading role in Hungary.

The bank's market share was 69 percent in retail loans, 69 percent in municipal loans and 11 percent in corporate credits, ICE said. OTP held 63.4 percent of retail, 89 percent of municipal and 14 percent of corporate deposits, ICE added.
OTP was one of the banks in the region which was down-sizing its workforce most effectively, the brokerage said.
OTP cut the real value of its personnel expenditure by some 23 percent in 1996, and planned workforce reductions were likely to result in further real savings in 1997, ICE said.
Regarding the quality of its loan portfolio, OTP's rigorous credit assessment had gained it one of the best records in the region, ICE said.
The brokerage added that retail current accounts, a sector in which OTP already had a dominant market share, had large growth potential in Hungary.
OTP holds some 1.58 million of the total two million such accounts in Hungary, which has an active workforce of five million, the brokerage said.
The changing habits of Hungarian retail banking customers were likely to enable OTP to boost its non-interest income by 24 percent in 1997 and 22 percent in 1998, ICE added.
The brokerage sees strong growth in OTP's earnings in 1997.

"Despite the moderate increase in net interest income, for 1997 we forecast 39 percent growth in earnings, mainly stemming from real savings in personnel expenditure and a significant reduction in the provision charge," it said.
"In 1998, we believe, earnings growth will slow down considerably; however OTP should continue to deliver a real growth in earning of between five and six percent."
Hungary targets inflation of around 17 percent in 1997 and some 12 percent in 1998.
